title: Replicating concept-vector steering on quantized models (does 4-bit break steering?)

original_idea.body:
# Replicating concept-vector steering on quantized models (does 4-bit break steering?)

**Problem:** Steering is usually studied on full-precision models, but real consumer/edge deployment uses 4-bit/8-bit quantization. Whether refusal/honesty steering vectors retain their effect under quantization is a practically important, unstudied replication.

**Direction:** Extract a steering vector on a full-precision open model, then apply it to 8-bit and 4-bit quantized versions of the same model, measuring how steering effectiveness and coherence degrade with precision. Twist: replicate steering across the quantization axis, which prior work ignores.

**Why it matters:** Quantized open models are what most independent users actually run. If steering-based safety silently breaks under quantization, edge deployments are unprotected — a diffuse, real-world gap that external researchers with one consumer GPU are perfectly placed to surface.

**Relevant context:** CAA / RepE steering methods; bitsandbytes 4-bit/8-bit quantization (standard on consumer GPUs); Beaglehole et al. stability open problem (extended to numeric precision).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (quantized edge deployments unprotected) but a gap to catastrophic-risk reduction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Steering across precision with bitsandbytes, standard tools, beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: same vector across precisions, clear effectiveness/coherence metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: consumer-GPU-relevant gap labs ignore, open models.

low_compute.reasoning: Quantized models lower memory; single consumer GPU, inference-only.

novelty.reasoning: Quantization+steering interaction appears largely unstudied; angle may be fairly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Steering under quantization appears mostly unstudied.
